column1: # Swiss Ephemeris 2.10.03, fixed star Sirius, from the crate's own catalogue (data/stars.tsv).
# Made by `cargo xtask fixtures stars`; don't edit.
# Mode jpl reads JPL DE440; swiss reads the Swiss Ephemeris' own files (before 1550,
# apparent: mode, jd_tt, right ascension, declination (of date, true equator and
#   equinox), ecliptic longitude, latitude (of date), degrees.
# icrs: mode, jd_tt, right ascension, declination, degrees: the apparent direction in
#   the axes of the ICRS (flags J2000 and ICRS: no precession or nutation), with light
#   deflection and aberration. It tests the reduction from the catalogue alone; the
#   positions of date also rest on the precession and nutation models, which the Swiss
#   Ephemeris sets itself (Vondrak 2011 and IAU 2000B by default).
# rise, set: site, jd_ut at which the search starts, jd_ut of the event; the star's
#   centre on the geometric horizon (no refraction), geocentric, mode as above.
#   Sites: Luxor 25.6995 N 32.6391 E 76 m; Heliopolis 30.1293 N 31.3075 E 25 m.
# heliacal: site, mode, astronomical year (Julian calendar before 1583), jd_ut at which the
#   search starts (1 January 0h UT), heliacal rising: start of visibility, optimum,
#   end (jd_ut), after the parameters used, which are:
# heliacal parameters: atmosphere pressure 1013.25 mbar, temperature 25.0 C, relative
# humidity 20 %, meteorological range 0 (computed from those); observer age 36,
# Snellen ratio 1, naked eye; flags: ephemeris mode, HELFLAG_VISLIM_NOMOON (the Moon
# not counted as a disturbance, so the date is the epoch's, not the year's); event
